plan_summary: Install and configure Nginx on Ubuntu 24.04 by updating system packages, adding the official repository key if necessary, installing the package, verifying the service status, and configuring basic security defaults.
assumptions: The host has network connectivity to download packages.
The user has sudo privileges to install software.

tasks.title: Update system package lists and upgrade existing packages
tasks.objective: Ensure the local package index is current before installing new software.
tasks.rationale: Running apt update prevents conflicts between old dependencies and new versions, ensuring a stable installation environment.
tasks.expected_output: Command completes with no errors or warnings regarding outdated packages.
success_criteria: The command returns to the prompt without error messages.

tasks.title: Verify Nginx repository availability or add official key
tasks.objective: Ensure the system can locate the Nginx package in the repositories.
tasks.rationale: Ubuntu 24.04 may require adding a specific signing key or repository source if not pre-configured for third-party packages like Nginx.
tasks.expected_output: Confirmation that the nginx package is available via 'apt search' or that the necessary keys are present.
success_criteria: 'apt search nginx' returns a valid package entry.

tasks.title: Install Nginx using the APT package manager
tasks.objective: Download and install the Nginx web server software.
tasks.rationale: This is the core installation step that places binaries, libraries, and configuration files onto the system.
tasks.expected_output: Nginx package installed with default configuration files created in /etc/nginx.
success_criteria: The command completes successfully without dependency errors.

tasks.title: Start the Nginx service and enable it to start on boot
tasks.objective: Launch the web server immediately and configure it for automatic startup.
tasks.rationale: Installation alone does not run the service; systemd commands are required to manage the process lifecycle.
tasks.expected_output: Nginx process running in the foreground or managed by systemd, and enabled for future boots.

tasks.title: Verify Nginx is listening on port 80
tasks.objective: Confirm the web server is accepting connections on the standard HTTP port.
tasks.rationale: Ensures the service is not only running but bound to the correct network interface and port.
tasks.expected_output: Output showing Nginx listening on 0.0.0.0:80 or specific IP:80.
success_criteria: The 'ss -tlnp' command lists port 80 associated with nginx.

tasks.title: Test HTTP connectivity using a browser or curl
tasks.objective: Validate that the web server responds to client requests with valid content.
tasks.rationale: Functional testing confirms that DNS resolution (if applicable) and HTTP responses are working correctly.
tasks.expected_output: A successful HTTP 200 response containing the default 'Welcome to nginx!' page or similar.
success_criteria: curl -I http://localhost returns an HTTP/1.1 200 OK status code.

tasks.title: Review and secure default configuration files
tasks.objective: Inspect the default site configuration to ensure no sensitive information is exposed.
tasks.rationale: Default configurations often expose server versions or paths that should be hidden for security best practices.
tasks.expected_output: A list of configuration files requiring review, specifically default.conf and sites-enabled/default.
success_criteria: The 'ls -la /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/' command lists the active configuration files.

tasks.title: Disable default site if not needed or configure virtual hosts
tasks.objective: Remove the default welcome page to prevent information leakage about the installation.
tasks.rationale: The default site often reveals 'Welcome to nginx!' which indicates a fresh install; removing it is a common security step.
tasks.expected_output: The default site configuration removed or replaced with a custom virtual host.
success_criteria: curl http://localhost no longer returns the default welcome page.

tasks.title: Configure firewall rules for port 80 and 443
tasks.objective: Ensure the system firewall allows traffic to the web server ports.
tasks.rationale: Even if Nginx is running, a host-based firewall (like UFW) might block incoming connections by default.
tasks.expected_output: Firewall rules updated to allow TCP traffic on ports 80 and optionally 443.

tasks.title: Document installation steps and verify final state
tasks.objective: Create a summary of the configuration and perform a final health check.
tasks.rationale: Documentation ensures reproducibility, and a final check confirms all subtasks were successful before closing the task.
tasks.expected_output: A brief log or note confirming Nginx is installed, running, and accessible.
success_criteria: All previous success criteria are met simultaneously.
